title: Add Minimum Number of Rungs
summary: Given a strictly increasing integer array representing ladder rung heights, starting from the floor at height 0, you must reach the last rung.
statement: Given a strictly increasing integer array representing ladder rung heights, starting from the floor at height 0, you must reach the last rung. You can only climb to the next rung if the distance is at most a specified value. You can add rungs at any positive integer height. Return the minimum number of rungs needed to be added to reach the last rung.
constraints: rungs has 1 through 100000 strictly increasing positive heights, each at most 1000000000.
Begin at floor height zero and insert rungs only at positive integer heights.
reference_solution:
def minimum_added_rungs(rungs, dist):
    answer = 0
    previous = 0
    for height in rungs:
        answer += (height - previous - 1) // dist
        previous = height
    return answer

hints: A gap of g needs exactly floor((g-1)/dist) inserted rungs.
Process each consecutive gap independently, including the gap from floor zero to the first rung.
Add (height-previous-1)//dist for every rung, then advance previous.
That many insertions divide a gap into the minimum number of pieces whose lengths are all at most dist; different gaps do not interact.
editorial: That many insertions divide a gap into the minimum number of pieces whose lengths are all at most dist; different gaps do not interact.

tests.explanation: The final gap needs two inserted rungs, such as heights seven and eight.
Every gap from the floor onward is already at most three, so no rung is added.
